text: Ramiriquí is a town and municipality located in the Colombian Department of Boyacá, within the Márquez Province subregion. It shares borders with Tunja to the north, Chinavita and Zetaquirá to the south, Rondón and Ciénaga to the east, and Chivatá, Tibaná, and Jenesano to the west. The town is named after the last cacique, Ramirique, and in the Chibcha language of the Muisca, "Ramirraquí" translates to "white earth"; an alternative etymology, "Ca-mi-quiquí," means "our strength over the grasslands." Before the arrival of Spanish conquistadors in the Altiplano Cundiboyacense during the 1530s, the area was inhabited by the Muisca people. The northern Muisca Confederation was later established in Hunza, present-day Tunja, following the mythological and violent cacique Goranchacha's relocation from Ramiriquí, with Hunzahúa becoming the first ruler of Hunza and the city being named after him. Quemuenchatocha, the second-last ruler of the Muisca, died in Ramiriquí after being defeated by Spanish conquistador Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada. The modern town was officially founded on December 21, 1541, by Spanish friar Pedro Durán. Petroglyphs have been discovered within the municipal boundaries. Key economic activities in Ramiriquí include agriculture—specifically uchuva, tree tomatoes, cucumbers, beans, blackberries, and maize—fishing, and crafts. Its geographic coordinates are 5°24′N 73°20′W (5.400°N 73.333°W).
